name: URTC-FLASHER
build: Standalone Python desktop tool. pip install -r requirements.txt; Qt Quick CAN-OTA deck is started with --qtquick.
notes: Real GUI flashing tool (CAN-OTA + full-chip SWD/JTAG). Qt Quick (`--qtquick`) is a real, full-parity front end for the entire workflow, not just CAN-OTA - CAN-OTA, read-only SWD/JTAG discovery, Board Snapshot, the 4 device-configuration writes, and full-chip SWD/JTAG programming (erase/write, dry run, back-up-before-erasing, RDP/option-byte check) all talk to the same production transport, validation and signed flashing code as the established Tkinter interface (31 real @Slot bindings in qt_flasher.py, cross-checked against assets/qml/FlasherDeck.qml's own controls - REV-032). Tkinter remains the default interface; nothing is Tkinter-only anymore. flasher_protocol.py's deadline/duration math uses time.monotonic() throughout, not the civil clock, so an NTP sync or manual clock change mid-flash can never shorten or lengthen a real timeout.
